title: Operational Intelligence Proof Backlog
summary: Current public-safe evidence still needed to strengthen the Operational Intelligence doctrine, Ravikanth Seri's professional representation, and the seri.ai product proof loop.
principle: The site should publish claims only as far as the evidence supports them, and unresolved proof gaps should be visible to serious reviewers.

items.claim: Experienced operators and architects can understand where Operational Intelligence begins, where it ends, and how to challenge it.
items.evidenceNeeded: Structured reviews from SRE, architecture, AI engineering, governance, executive, and product reviewers using the practitioner review form.
items.currentEvidence: The Evidence Pack defines reviewer roles, dimension verdicts, evidence ledger fields, and doctrine impact categories, and the First-Time Visitor Review Kit plus the Practitioner Review Packet now give reviewers an explicit path from Start Here to Contact. The beta feedback form now captures whether visitors can explain Ravikanth, name the thesis, identify the proof path completed, state confidence, name inspected evidence, and say what evidence would change their mind. The practitioner review form also captures first-impression verdict, person-work fit, thesis clarity, proof route, artifact recall, and demo feeling as bounded categories.
items.nextProof: Run the Practitioner Review Packet with at least five public-safe practitioner or first-time visitor reviews that identify what was clear, what was confusing, strongest claim, weakest claim, evidence needed, implementation questions, and whether the site represents Ravikanth without generic self-promotion.
items.wouldChange: If reviewers cannot distinguish the model from observability, AIOps, ITIL, incident command, or chatbot-only assistance, revise the doctrine boundaries.

items.claim: The Operational Intelligence workflow improves reviewability compared with dashboard-only, chatbot-only, and ticket-only investigation modes.
items.evidenceNeeded: Same-facts OI-ROOM-001 comparison runs scored on evidence completeness, contradiction handling, missing-evidence honesty, hypothesis quality, decision safety, replayability, and reviewer confidence.
items.currentEvidence: Run 001 of the control comparison was executed on 2026-08-26 and published at /publication-pack/oi-room-001-control-comparison-run-001.md. It scores four modes across the seven dimensions and returned two findings unfavourable to the doctrine: dashboard-only scores equal on numeric evidence completeness, and the protocol's own stated cost risk is still untested. The run was performed by the author of the workflow under test, on a case he also authored, so it carries no independence.
items.nextProof: Have an independent practitioner author a case and re-run the comparison. Run 001's largest stated limitation is that the case contains exactly the features the workflow handles, so an externally authored case is the specific evidence that would make the result meaningful.
items.wouldChange: If the workflow adds structure without improving judgment, simplify the model or narrow claims to the cases where structure helps.

items.claim: Ask Ravikanth is a useful interface to Ravikanth Seri's verified public professional graph rather than a generic chatbot wrapper.
items.evidenceNeeded: Reviewer-labeled Ask sessions across professional profile, doctrine, architecture, evidence, routing, unknown questions, and public-safety boundaries.
items.currentEvidence: Deterministic Ask fixtures, rubric dimensions, citation expectations, refusal behavior, local fallback behavior, and the Ask live review packet are validated in the build.
items.nextProof: Run the Ask live review packet with external reviewers to compare local fallback, vector retrieval, and model synthesis on the same safe prompt set using only category, latency, success, failure, source count, checked artifacts, and reviewer verdict metadata.
items.wouldChange: If Ask cannot cite relevant public sources or separate fact from inference under realistic questions, reduce answer scope and improve retrieval before expanding claims.

items.claim: seri.ai can operate as a stable public beta with useful fallbacks when optional AI or database services are unavailable.
items.evidenceNeeded: Deployment observations for uptime, build health, route availability, Ask latency, fallback rate, contact failure rate, and privacy-safe analytics events.
items.currentEvidence: Deployment validators, API timeout handling, local fallbacks, rate limiting, analytics contracts, rendered-route validation, and performance budgets are enforced locally.
items.nextProof: After Vercel beta deployment, review production logs and analytics using only privacy-safe metadata and publish limitations in the release report or scorecard.
items.wouldChange: If fallback rate, route errors, or latency make review unreliable, prioritize reliability fixes before deeper publication work.

items.claim: The site feels publication-grade on mobile, tablet, and desktop for first-time executives, engineers, recruiters, and founders.
items.evidenceNeeded: Durable screenshots, touch walkthrough notes, and keyboard walkthrough notes for the homepage, Ask Ravikanth, Operations Room, Work, Background, Doctrine, Radar, and Evidence Pack at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.
items.currentEvidence: Source-level viewport contracts, accessibility validation, rendered-route checks, performance budgets, browser-controlled mobile/tablet/desktop route checks, 27 durable first-viewport screenshots, source-validated mobile touch walkthrough notes for Ask, Operations Room, Doctrine, Radar, and Work, and source-validated keyboard accessibility walkthrough notes for Ask and Operations Room.
items.nextProof: Run physical-device touch checks, browser-recorded keyboard tab-order checks, assistive-technology or screen-reader checks, and external hierarchy/density review, then convert any concrete failures into regression checks.
items.wouldChange: If the Operations Room or homepage still feels like a demo at realistic viewports, reduce visual noise and sharpen first-task clarity without changing the architecture.

items.claim: Ravikanth Seri remains unmistakably the author, engineer, and professional identity behind the Operational Intelligence body of work.
items.evidenceNeeded: Approved portrait or identity asset, verified profile links, resume provenance, public-code links, LinkedIn signal, and a first-viewport path from person to work to evidence.
items.currentEvidence: The homepage, Start Here, Work, Resume, /background, GitHub link, LinkedIn link, production-delivery chain, durable non-photographic public identity mark, approved portrait intake contract, approved portrait rendered on professional-orientation surfaces, and structured first-time feedback form connect the person to the public body of work. First-impression review capture now records person-work fit, thesis clarity, proof route, artifact recall, and demo feeling as categorical evidence instead of relying only on prose feedback.
items.nextProof: Run external first-impression review to verify that the person-work-evidence path feels clear, credible, and specific to Ravikanth rather than anonymous.
items.wouldChange: If visitors still experience the site as an anonymous product, rebalance homepage and navigation copy toward Ravikanth as author without turning it into self-promotion.

items.claim: Public repositories and project pages can demonstrate Ravikanth Seri's engineering judgment only when they expose inspectable design choices, boundaries, and review questions without implying private production adoption.
items.evidenceNeeded: Reviewer walkthroughs that inspect the GitHub profile, the user-authorized Sentinalai public repository reference, Work, Projects, and the Public Project Proof Ledger for runnable examples, public-safe architecture boundaries, and what each artifact does or does not prove.
items.currentEvidence: Work, Projects, the Public Project Proof Ledger, the public-code review rubric, Sentinalai inspection path, Ask and Search routing, and content validation define what reviewers should inspect. Do not infer repository metrics, production adoption, private deployment, private integrations, or live incident outcomes from public code alone.
items.nextProof: Run the project proof review questions with external reviewers, improve the representative public repository README or runnable walkthroughs only with public-safe details, and publish dimension-level findings without private metrics.
items.wouldChange: If reviewers cannot tell what the public code proves, or if they infer production adoption, private integrations, or live incident outcomes from repository presence, narrow the claim and strengthen the public-code boundary.
